text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short, focused periods called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Each day begins with a quick standup meeting, where team members share what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any problems they face. Before each sprint, the team chooses tasks from a prioritized list called the backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe a feature from the perspective of the end user. This iterative development allows teams to receive feedback regularly, make improvements, and deliver value to customers more quickly and effectively.
